---
title: "Practical 1: Time series objects in R on AAPL data"
date: 2026-08-17
---

In this practical I first worked through the Base R `ts()` code from the class slides, and then applied the same steps to real data. I used the daily closing prices of AAPL for 2019 from the S&P 500 dataset, which is about 252 trading days.

**Base R fundamentals.** I used `window()` to take a subset of a series by time period, `diff()` to difference it and `lag()` to shift it. With `lag()` I learnt that it shifts the time labels of a series and not the values, so a lagged series and the original do not line up on their own. If you combine them with `cbind()` you end up comparing the wrong pairs of observations without any error telling you. `ts.union()` lines them up by their time index. I also compared `plot.ts()` with the normal `plot()` for `ts` objects, and used `decompose()` to split a series into trend, seasonal and remainder parts. The weakness of `decompose()` is at the start and end of the series, because the centred moving average it uses cannot be calculated there.

**Applying this to real data.** For the AAPL data I made a Base R `ts` object with `frequency = 252`. Daily stock data has no rows for weekends or public holidays, so using 365 would have made the seasonal index drift out of line over time. I also made a `tsibble` version to use with `feasts`.

This is where I ran into a problem. Calling `ACF()` on the tsibble gave an "implicit gaps" error. The tsibble was indexed by calendar date, so it treated every weekend and public holiday as a missing observation, even though the market is closed on those days. I fixed it by adding a `trading_day` column with `row_number()` and using that as the index instead. I kept `date` as a normal column so I could still use it in plots. After this `ACF()` and `STL()` ran.

The fix caused a second problem. With `trading_day` as the index, `autoplot()` of the STL components showed trading day numbers on the x axis instead of dates. To get the dates back I built the plot myself in `ggplot2`. I joined a lookup table of `trading_day` and `date` onto the STL `components()` output, then used `scale_x_date()` and `facet_grid()` to make the multi panel plot with monthly date labels. For STL I set the seasonal period to 5, which is one trading week.

**Takeaway:** `ts` and `tsibble` objects handle the time index very differently, and this decides which functions will run at all, as the `ACF()` error showed. For daily stock data the index has to follow trading days and not the calendar. STL was also the better choice over `decompose()`, since it uses Loess and does not lose the start and end of the series.
